scope: All seven steps of the measured OIM nickel detector-pattern inspection example; zero-based indices.

filters.purpose: Read measured Scan 1 with detector patterns in acquisition order. Retain imported orientations without frame corrections because this example inspects detector data and indexing metrics, not specimen-direction orientations. Z spacing 1 is a single-slice placeholder.
Record zero-based acquisition tuple identity 0..28085 as uint32 before cropping. X varies fastest, so SourceScanIndex = y * 186 + x for this scan.

Copy the adjacent acquisition-grid cells (67,10) and (68,10), inclusive, with every cell array and pattern kept in the same order. Preserve the full scalar map for context; no resampling, feature renumbering, or detector-pixel crop.

After copying the selected patterns, remove the full-map Pattern array (101109600 bytes) and both geometries' unpopulated X Position/Y Position arrays. This reader creates those coordinate arrays but leaves zeros for this input, so retain source scan IDs and geometry origin/spacing instead. Original HDF5 and import peak memory are unchanged.
Write Pattern.bin: two consecutive 60 by 60 uint8 detector images, pattern then row then column, 7200 bytes with no header. Endianness has no effect on one-byte uint8. This is not an EDAX UP1 file.

Export both selected rows, including tuple zero, in the same order as Pattern.bin: source tuple index, Confidence Index, Image Quality, and Fit. Recover acquisition-grid x=index%186 and y=index//186; these are grid indices, not detector-pixel or physical coordinates. These metrics do not establish indexing validity.
Save the full scalar acquisition map, original imported Euler/phase context, and selected two-pattern geometry. Use this metadata-bearing file alongside the raw binary and two-row manifest.
